database_limit: Commander Spellbook is incomplete, especially for new cards. No-match records are evidence, not proof of absence.
notes: Smaug was scanned and manually reviewed on 2026-09-08. All 10 existing mains and Gandalf’s nine-card switch were freshly exported and verified unchanged; their hash-matching scan and individual review dates are retained. Included database results are adjudicated individually; finite effects are not relabeled infinite. Database omissions and manual screening do not prove combo completeness.

decks.summary: The 2026-09-05 exact-list scan returned no included combo. Balmor adds finite instant/sorcery combat scaling, Tocasia's Welcome triggers only once each turn, and Cosmic Rebirth is a one-shot recursion spell. Jeskai Ascendancy and mana creatures still lack a repeatable spell or bounce engine; the nearby buyback, Freed from the Real, and Intruder Alarm templates have missing named cards.

The 2026-09-05 exact-list scan returned no included combo. Devoted Druid has left the deck. Bala Ged Recovery and Bridgeworks Battle add two spell/land MDFCs, while Hammer of Nazahn and Krosan Grip add protection and interaction. Selvala, Bear Umbra, Pip-Boy 3000, Shifting Woodland, and the Equipment-copy package still lack a repeatable untap or extra-combat loop; the Hammer/Apex Altisaur candidate lacks Apex Altisaur.

The refreshed exact-list scan returned no included combo. Hobbit Hole replaces Terramorphic Expanse without adding a repeatable Food, life-gain, sacrifice, or historic-card recursion loop; The One Ring and the Food/Hobbit engines remain finite.

The posted Maximum Flavor main deck returned no included combo and contains neither Surge to Victory nor Savage Beating. Its exact nine-for-nine Maximum Power switch adds both cards plus Solve the Equation, restoring the deck's intentional conditional unlimited-combat finish only in the Maximum Power configuration.

decks.summary: The 2026-09-05 exact-list scan returned no included combo. Abjure and Flare of Denial provide one-shot sacrifice costs; Flare requires a nontoken blue creature and cannot sacrifice an Illusion token. Flow of Knowledge and the two Thirst spells improve finite instant-speed draw/discard. Manual review of Minn, Illusion copies, the Altars, Blasting Station, and draw engines found no unrestricted return-and-sacrifice cycle. The nearby Meloku, Fool's Demise, persist/undying, and Lyla templates remain incomplete. Teferi, Master of Time can take two consecutive extra turns via its ultimate, which remains a separate pregame disclosure.

All three returned Apex Altisaur and Wrathful Raptors lines are present. They clear opposing creatures and can deal near-infinite damage when opposing bodies keep Apex Altisaur's fight chain going; Savage Order is the compact tutored version and is the list's main Bracket 3 disclosure.

The 2026-09-05 exact-list scan again returned the finite Fire Covenant and Brash Taunter kill. Fighter Class improves Sunforger access, while Galadriel's Dismissal, Tibalt's Trickery, Nils, and Combat Calligrapher add finite interaction or combat incentives. The five-card Arcbond loop remains present: copy Arcbond onto Brash Taunter and Selfless Squire, resolve the Squire's enter trigger that turn, make both indestructible, then have Brash fight the Squire. No new complete loop was identified among the changed cards.

lines.reason: Resolve Selfless Squire's enter trigger this turn to prevent damage to you. Copy Arcbond so Brash Taunter and the Squire each have its delayed trigger, give both indestructible with Boros Charm, and activate Brash Taunter to fight the Squire while it can tap. Each Arcbond trigger damages the other creature and creates the next trigger; the prevention effect protects you while opponents take each iteration.

Sylvan Library and Tamiyo's Safekeeping replace Strionic Resonator and The Shire, adding selection and protection without a repeatable untap or creature-recast engine. The 2026-09-05 exact-list scan returned no included combo. Molten Echoes has left the deck. Chronicle of Victory adds cast-based draw and combat pressure; Priest of Ancient Lore adds a Dwarf enter trigger; Ascend from Avernus and Sevinne's Reclamation add finite recovery and exile after their relevant graveyard use. Thorin, Bifur, Panharmonicon, Anointed Procession, Cadric, and Fíli still multiply triggers, tokens, and Treasures finitely. The closest Reaver Cleaver, Magda, and Thorin, Company's Leader loops lack Aggravated Assault, Hellkite Charger, or a repeatable untap engine.

Intentional Bracket 4 Treasure combo. Nine included candidates were checked individually. Mayhem Devil, Havoc Jester, Chain Lightning, and Dizzying Gaze supply repeatable engines; Blazing Sunsteel is an additional manually confirmed line. Pyrohemia/Pestilence are life-limited without support, Inheritance/Act is finite optional access, Dawnsire/Pain is a finite 100-damage burst, and Dawnsire/Fiendlash was corrected to power-based damage. The estimate’s abstract prepare templates are not satisfied by this list; it contains no prepare card.

lines.reason: Dawnsire needs at least ten charge counters and a creature able to attack. Pain for All must enchant a creature you control; Smaug is the durable in-list host. Attack with any creature, target that enchanted creature with the Dawnsire trigger, then Pain for All deals 100 to each opponent. This is a finite damage burst, not an infinite loop. Smaug also creates 100 Treasures.

Start with both creatures on the battlefield and an untapped Treasure. Sacrifice the Treasure for mana, target Smaug with the sacrifice trigger, and resolve Smaug’s replacement Treasure. Repeat to bank mana while keeping one Treasure. The base loop uses its damage on Smaug; a separate entry/sacrifice payoff or damage amplifier supplies lethal output.

Start with both creatures on the battlefield and an untapped Treasure. Sacrifice the Treasure for mana, target Smaug with the sacrifice trigger, and resolve Smaug’s replacement Treasure. Repeat to bank mana while keeping one Treasure. The base loop uses its damage on Smaug; a separate entry/sacrifice payoff or damage amplifier supplies lethal output.

Blasphemous Act deals 13 damage per creature. Each damaged creature produces one optional Inheritance trigger for its controller to exile that many cards and play them until the end of their next turn. The amount is bounded by damaged creatures and library size; opponents can benefit too. No repeatable loop or guaranteed library-wide access follows from these two cards alone.

Pay one red mana to damage every creature and player, resolve Smaug’s one Treasure, then spend it to repeat. The base line breaks even on mana but damages its controller and kills unprotected support creatures. It is finite at an ordinary life total, can cause its pilot to lose, and needs a life advantage or additional protection/payoff to secure a win. Lifelink on Smaug does not grant lifelink to the enchantment.

The base line breaks even on mana but damages its controller and kills unprotected support creatures. It is finite at an ordinary life total, can cause its pilot to lose, and needs a life advantage or additional protection/payoff to secure a win. Lifelink on Smaug does not grant lifelink to the enchantment.

Have RRR available with Smaug on the battlefield. Spend R to cast Chain Lightning at Smaug and pay the first RR to copy it during resolution, before the first Treasure trigger resolves. Resolve that trigger above the copy to make three Treasures. Each later copy makes three and costs two Treasures to continue, leaving one extra per iteration. Declining the copy payment ends the loop; separate payoffs convert the engine to lethal output.

The database description incorrectly says Fiendlash repeats Dawnsire’s 100 damage. Current Oracle instead deals damage equal to the equipped creature’s power to one player or planeswalker. With ten charge counters, a legal attacker, and Fiendlash on otherwise unmodified 8-power Smaug, Dawnsire deals 100 to Smaug, Smaug makes 100 Treasures, and Fiendlash deals 10 to one target. This is finite, and 100 damage to that target is not established.

Enchant Smaug and start with R. Smaug has flying, so the granted ability can target himself. One damage makes one Treasure, whose red mana funds the next activation. No tap cost is involved. The base loop is mana-neutral; Xorn, Goldspan Dragon, Crime Novelist, or Roaming Throne naming Dragon creates a surplus. In-list damage or token payoffs make it lethal.

Equip Smaug and deal him noncombat damage with an enabler. Aim each Sunsteel trigger back at Smaug and resolve Treasure triggers along the way. Indestructible lets him survive repeated damage. Choose a different target to end the cycle. Entry/sacrifice payoffs, Pain for All, or Fiendlash convert it into lethal output. This line was not among the nine included database results.

decks.payoff_review: Reckless Fireweaver and Weftstalker Ardent trigger on artifact entries; Mirkwood Bats triggers on token creation and sacrifice; Marionette Apprentice, Disciple of the Vault, and The Sackville-Bagginses convert artifact/token sacrifices to life loss. Pain for All and Fiendlash convert repeated damage to Smaug to opponent damage. Heroes for Hire, Professional Face-Breaker, and optional Expedited Inheritance provide finite library access from repeatable resources. Payoffs must remain on the battlefield; sweepers can kill support creatures before Treasures enter.
decks.primer_review: Public primer read 2026-09-08 mentions Agent of the Iron Throne, Torment of Hailfire, and Witch’s Clinic, which are absent from the exact current export. They were not counted as cards or prerequisites. Moxfield was not edited.
